verses.20:4: Now it came about after this that war arose at Gezer with the Philistines. At that time Sibbechai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, who was of the descendants of the giants, and they were subdued.
verses.20:5: And again there was war with the Philistines, and Elhanan the son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
verses.20:6: Yet again there was war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature whose fingers and toes were six and six, twenty-four in all; and he also was born to the giant.
verses.20:7: When he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea, the brother of David, struck him down.
verses.20:8: These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.21:1: Now Satan stood up against Israel and incited David to number Israel.
verses.21:2: So David said to Joab and to the leaders of the people, "Go, number Israel from Beersheba even to Dan, and bring it to me, that I may know their number."
verses.21:3: And Joab said, "May the LORD add to His people a hundred times as many as they are! My lord the king, are they not all servants to my lord? Why does my lord seek this thing? Why should he be a cause of guilt to Israel?"
verses.21:4: Yet the king's word prevailed against Joab. Therefore Joab went forth and went throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
verses.21:5: Then Joab gave the sum of the numbering of the people to David. And all Israel was one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Judah was four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.21:6: But he did not muster Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king's command was abhorrent to Joab.
verses.21:7: And this thing was evil in the sight of God, and He struck Israel.
verses.21:8: So David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in doing this thing; now, I pray, put away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.21:9: Then the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying,
verses.21:10: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'Thus says the LORD: Three things I hold out before you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
verses.21:11: So Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Choose for yourself,
verses.21:12: either three years of famine, or three months to be swept away before your adversaries while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or else three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, with the angel of the LORD bringing destruction throughout all the territory of Israel.' Now therefore consider what word I shall bring back to Him who sent me."
verses.21:13: And David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let me fall, I pray, into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are exceedingly great; but do not let me fall into the hand of man."
verses.21:14: So the LORD sent pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
verses.21:15: And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it; and as he was destroying, the LORD looked and relented concerning the calamity, and said to the destroying angel, "It is enough; now stay your hand." And the angel of the LORD was standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:16: Then David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with his drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. So David and the elders, covered in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.
verses.21:17: And David said to God, "Was it not I who gave the command to number the people? Indeed, it is I who have sinned and done exceedingly wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? O LORD my God, let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father's house, and not against Your people as a plague."
verses.21:18: Then the angel of the LORD commanded Gad to say to David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.21:19: So David went up at the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the LORD.
verses.21:20: Now Ornan turned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves; and Ornan was threshing wheat.
verses.21:21: So David came to Ornan; and Ornan looked and saw David, and he went out from the threshing floor and bowed down before David with his face to the ground.
verses.21:22: Then David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of the threshing floor, that I may build on it an altar to the LORD. Give it to me for the full price, that the plague may be held back from the people."
verses.21:23: And Ornan said to David, "Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good in his sight. Behold, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering; I give it all."
verses.21:24: Then King David said to Ornan, "No, I will surely purchase it for the full price, for I will not take what belongs to you for the LORD, nor offer up a burnt offering without cost."
verses.21:25: So David gave Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.
verses.21:26: And David built there an altar to the LORD, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings; and he called upon the LORD, and He answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering.
verses.21:27: So the LORD commanded the angel, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
verses.21:28: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered sacrifice there.
verses.21:29: For the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
verses.21:30: But David could not go before it to inquire of God, for he was terrified because of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
verses.22:1: Then David said, "This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."
verses.22:2: So David commanded that the sojourners who were in the land of Israel be gathered together; and he appointed stonecutters to hew dressed stones to build the house of God.
verses.22:3: David also prepared iron in abundance for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and bronze in abundance beyond weight;
verses.22:4: and cedar timbers without number, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought cedar timbers in abundance to David.
verses.22:5: For David said, "Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly grand, of renown and glory throughout all the lands; let me therefore make preparation for it." So David made abundant preparation before his death.
verses.22:6: Then he called for Solomon his son, and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.22:7: And David said to Solomon, "My son, as for me, it was in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.
verses.22:8: But the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 'You have shed blood in abundance and have waged great wars; you shall not build a house for My name, because you have shed much blood upon the earth before Me.
verses.22:9: Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. For Solomon shall be his name, and I will bestow peace and quietness upon Israel in his days.
verses.22:10: He shall build a house for My name, and he shall be a son to Me, and I will be a Father to him; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
verses.22:11: Now, my son, may the LORD be with you; and may you prosper, and build the house of the LORD your God, just as He has spoken concerning you.
verses.22:12: Only may the LORD grant you discretion and understanding, and appoint you over Israel, that you may keep the law of the LORD your God.
verses.22:13: Then you shall prosper, if you are careful to observe the statutes and the judgments which the LORD commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous; do not fear, nor be dismayed.
verses.22:14: Now behold, in my affliction I have prepared for the house of the LORD one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for they are in great abundance; timber and stone also I have prepared, and you may add to them.
verses.22:15: Moreover, there are workmen with you in abundance—stonecutters, and craftsmen in stone and wood, and every skilled person for every kind of work.
verses.22:16: Of the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron there is no number. Arise and act, and may the LORD be with you."
verses.22:17: David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to assist Solomon his son:
verses.22:18: "Is not the LORD your God with you? And has He not given you rest on every side? For He has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before His people.
verses.22:19: Now set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the name of the LORD."
verses.23:1: Now David was old and full of days, and he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
verses.23:2: And he gathered together all the leaders of Israel, with the priests and the Levites.
verses.23:3: Now the Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward; and their count by head, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
verses.23:4: Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD, and six thousand were officers and judges;
verses.23:5: and four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand were praising the LORD with the instruments which I made for giving praise.
verses.23:6: Then David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.23:7: Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
verses.23:8: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel—three.
verses.23:9: The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran—three. These were the heads of the fathers' houses of Ladan.
verses.23:10: And the sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
verses.23:11: Now Jahath was the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became a single father's house in one reckoning.
verses.23:12: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four.
verses.23:13: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to Him, and to bless in His name forever.
verses.23:14: Now as for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi.
verses.23:15: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
verses.23:16: The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief.
verses.23:17: And the sons of Eliezer were Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah became exceedingly numerous.
verses.23:18: The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
verses.23:19: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
verses.23:20: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
verses.23:21: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
verses.23:22: And Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters; so their brethren, the sons of Kish, took them as wives.
verses.23:23: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three.
verses.23:24: These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' houses—the heads of the fathers' houses as they were enrolled, by the count of names head by head—who performed the work for the service of the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:25: For David said, "The LORD God of Israel has given rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever,
verses.23:26: and as for the Levites also, they will no longer have to carry the tabernacle or any of its vessels for its service."
verses.23:27: For by the last words of David, the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward.
verses.23:28: For their station was alongside the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the LORD, in charge of the courts and the chambers, and the purifying of every holy thing, and the work of the service of the house of God,
verses.23:29: and for the showbread, and for the fine flour for the grain offering, and for the unleavened wafers, and for what is prepared on the griddle, and for what is mixed, and for all measures of capacity and size;
verses.23:30: and to stand morning by morning to give thanks and to praise the LORD, and likewise at evening;
verses.23:31: and at every offering of burnt offerings to the LORD on the Sabbaths, on the New Moons, and at the appointed feasts, by number according to the ordinance prescribed for them, continually before the LORD.
verses.23:32: And they were to keep the charge of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the holy place, and the charge of the sons of Aaron their brethren, for the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:1: Now these were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.24:2: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; therefore Eleazar and Ithamar ministered as priests.
verses.24:3: And David, along with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divided them according to their appointed order in their service.
verses.24:4: More chief men were found among the sons of Eleazar than among the sons of Ithamar, and thus they divided them: among the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen heads of fathers' houses, and among the sons of Ithamar eight according to their fathers' houses.
verses.24:5: Thus they divided them by lots, one group alike with the other; for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God both of the sons of Eleazar and of the sons of Ithamar.
verses.24:6: And Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, one of the Levites, recorded them in the presence of the king, the leaders, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites—one father's house taken for Eleazar, and one taken in turn for Ithamar.
verses.24:7: Now the first lot came out for Jehoiarib, the second for Jedaiah,
verses.24:8: the third for Harim, the fourth for Seorim,
verses.24:9: the fifth for Malchijah, the sixth for Mijamin,
verses.24:10: the seventh for Hakkoz, the eighth for Abijah,
verses.24:11: the ninth for Jeshua, the tenth for Shecaniah,
verses.24:12: the eleventh for Eliashib, the twelfth for Jakim,
verses.24:13: the thirteenth for Huppah, the fourteenth for Jeshebeab,
verses.24:14: the fifteenth for Bilgah, the sixteenth for Immer,
verses.24:15: the seventeenth for Hezir, the eighteenth for Happizzez,
verses.24:16: the nineteenth for Pethahiah, the twentieth for Jehezkel,
verses.24:17: the twenty-first for Jachin, the twenty-second for Gamul,
verses.24:18: the twenty-third for Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth for Maaziah.
verses.24:19: This was their appointed order for their service, to come into the house of the LORD according to their regulation by the hand of Aaron their father, just as the LORD God of Israel had commanded him.
verses.24:20: Now concerning the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
verses.24:21: Concerning Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah was the chief.
verses.24:22: Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
verses.24:23: And the sons: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
verses.24:24: The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
verses.24:25: The brother of Micah was Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
verses.24:26: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
verses.24:27: The sons of Merari by Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
verses.24:28: Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
verses.24:29: Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
verses.24:30: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their fathers' houses.
verses.24:31: These also cast lots just as their brethren the sons of Aaron did, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the priests and the Levites—the chief father's house just like his younger brother.
verses.25:1: Moreover, David and the commanders of the host set apart for the service some of the sons of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, with harps, and with cymbals. And this was the number of the workmen according to their service:
verses.25:2: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah; the sons of Asaph were under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied at the direction of the king.
verses.25:3: Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun with the lyre, who prophesied in giving thanks and praising the LORD.
verses.25:4: Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
verses.25:5: All these were the sons of Heman, the king's seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. For God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
verses.25:6: All these were under the direction of their father for singing in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God; Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the authority of the king.
verses.25:7: So their number, together with their brethren who were trained in singing to the LORD, all who were skillful, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
verses.25:8: And they cast lots for their duties alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher with the pupil.
verses.25:9: Now the first lot came out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he with his brethren and his sons, twelve.
verses.25:10: The third to Zaccur, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:11: The fourth to Izri, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:12: The fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:13: The sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:14: The seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:15: The eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:16: The ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:17: The tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:18: The eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:19: The twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:20: The thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:21: The fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:22: The fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:23: The sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:24: The seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:25: The eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:26: The nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:27: The twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:28: The twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:29: The twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:30: The twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.25:31: The twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brethren, twelve.
verses.26:1: Concerning the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
verses.26:2: And Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
verses.26:3: Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
verses.26:4: Moreover, Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
verses.26:5: Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him.
verses.26:6: Also to Shemaiah his son were born sons who held authority over their father's house, for they were mighty men of valor.
verses.26:7: The sons of Shemaiah were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose brethren Elihu and Semachiah were men of valor.
verses.26:8: All these were of the sons of Obed-Edom, they and their sons and their brethren, able men with strength for the service: sixty-two of Obed-Edom.
verses.26:9: And Meshelemiah had sons and brethren, valiant men, eighteen.
verses.26:10: Also Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief—for though he was not the firstborn, his father appointed him chief—
verses.26:11: Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth; all the sons and brethren of Hosah were thirteen.
verses.26:12: To these divisions of the gatekeepers, to the chief men, belonged duties corresponding to those of their brethren, to minister in the house of the LORD.
verses.26:13: And they cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their fathers' houses, for every gate.
verses.26:14: And the lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. Then they cast lots for Zechariah his son, a counselor of understanding, and his lot came out for the north;
verses.26:15: to Obed-Edom, the south; and to his sons, the storehouse.
verses.26:16: To Shuppim and Hosah, the west, with the Gate of Shallecheth on the ascending highway, watch opposite watch.
verses.26:17: On the east were six Levites, on the north four each day, on the south four each day, and for the storehouse two by two.
verses.26:18: As for the colonnade on the west, there were four on the highway and two at the colonnade.
verses.26:19: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the sons of the Korahites and among the sons of Merari.
verses.26:20: And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of God and over the treasuries of the dedicated things.
verses.26:21: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
verses.26:22: The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and Joel his brother, were over the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
verses.26:23: Of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
verses.26:24: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was chief overseer over the treasuries.
verses.26:25: And his brethren by Eliezer were Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
verses.26:26: This Shelomoth and his brethren were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things which King David, and the heads of the fathers' houses, the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army, had dedicated.
verses.26:27: Out of the battles and out of the spoil they dedicated these things to maintain the house of the LORD.
verses.26:28: And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated—whatever anyone had dedicated—was under the hand of Shelomith and his brethren.
verses.26:29: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed for the outside work over Israel, as officers and judges.
verses.26:30: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, one thousand seven hundred able men, had the oversight of Israel on the side of the Jordan westward, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
verses.26:31: Among the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites according to his generations by fathers' houses. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought out, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.
verses.26:32: And his brethren, valiant men, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers' houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for every matter of the king.
verses.27:1: Now the children of Israel according to their number—the heads of the fathers' houses, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter of the divisions that came in and went out month by month through all the months of the year—each division was twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:2: Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:3: He was of the sons of Perez, the chief of all the commanders of the armies for the first month.
verses.27:4: Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and of his division Mikloth was also the leader; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:5: The third commander of the army for the third month was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest, as chief; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:6: This was the Benaiah who was a mighty man among the thirty and was over the thirty; and over his division was Ammizabad his son.
verses.27:7: The fourth for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:8: The fifth for the fifth month was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:9: The sixth for the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:10: The seventh for the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:11: The eighth for the eighth month was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:12: The ninth for the ninth month was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjaminites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:13: The tenth for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:14: The eleventh for the eleventh month was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:15: The twelfth for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
verses.27:16: Now over the tribes of Israel: over the Reubenites the chief officer was Eliezer the son of Zichri; over the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah;
verses.27:17: over Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; over Aaron, Zadok;
verses.27:18: over Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; over Issachar, Omri the son of Michael;
verses.27:19: over Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; over Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel;
verses.27:20: over the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; over the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah;
verses.27:21: over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; over Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner;
verses.27:22: over Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the leaders of the tribes of Israel.
verses.27:23: Yet David did not take a count of those from twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said He would multiply Israel like the stars of the heavens.
verses.27:24: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number them, yet he did not finish, for wrath came upon Israel because of this; nor was the number entered in the account of the chronicles of King David.
verses.27:25: Over the king's treasuries was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah.
verses.27:26: Over those who did the work of the field for tilling the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub.
verses.27:27: Over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; and over the produce of the vineyards for the wine storehouses was Zabdi the Shiphmite.
verses.27:28: Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowlands was Baal-Hanan the Gederite; and over the storehouses of oil was Joash.
verses.27:29: Over the herds grazing in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite; and over the herds in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai.
verses.27:30: Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the female donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite.
verses.27:31: Over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the officials over the property that belonged to King David.
verses.27:32: Also Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king's sons.
verses.27:33: Ahithophel was the king's counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend.
verses.27:34: After Ahithophel were Jehoiada the son of Benaiah and Abiathar; and the commander of the king's army was Joab.
verses.28:1: Now David assembled at Jerusalem all the officials of Israel: the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions who served the king, the commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and the stewards over all the property and livestock belonging to the king and his sons, together with the court officers, the mighty men, and every valiant warrior.
verses.28:2: Then King David rose to his feet and said, "Hear me, my brethren and my people: I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD and for the footstool of our God, and I had made preparations to build it.
verses.28:3: But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for My name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'
verses.28:4: Yet the LORD God of Israel chose me from all my father's house to be king over Israel forever; for He chose Judah to be the ruler, and of the house of Judah, the house of my father, and among my father's sons He was pleased with me to make me king over all Israel.
verses.28:5: And of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—He has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
verses.28:6: And He said to me, 'Solomon your son, he shall build My house and My courts; for I have chosen him to be My son, and I will be a Father to him.
verses.28:7: Moreover I will establish his kingdom forever, if he remains steadfast to do My commandments and My judgments, as it is this day.'
verses.28:8: Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.
verses.28:9: And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father, and serve Him with an undivided heart and a willing soul; for the LORD searches all hearts and discerns every intent of the thoughts. If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever.
verses.28:10: Take heed now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary; be strong, and do it."
verses.28:11: Then David gave his son Solomon the pattern for the vestibule, its buildings, its treasuries, its upper chambers, its inner rooms, and the room of the mercy seat;
verses.28:12: and the pattern of all that he had by the Spirit, for the courts of the house of the LORD, for all the chambers all around, for the treasuries of the house of God, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things;
verses.28:13: also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the vessels of service in the house of the LORD:
verses.28:14: he gave gold by weight for the things of gold, for all vessels of every kind of service; and for all vessels of silver by weight, for all vessels of every kind of service;
verses.28:15: and the weight for the lampstands of gold and their lamps of gold, by weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and for the lampstands of silver by weight, for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
verses.28:16: and the gold by weight for the tables of the showbread, for each table, and silver for the tables of silver;
verses.28:17: also pure gold for the forks, the basins, and the pitchers; and for the golden bowls, by weight for each bowl, and for the silver bowls, by weight for each bowl;
verses.28:18: and refined gold by weight for the altar of incense, and gold for the pattern of the chariot—the cherubim that spread out their wings and overshadowed the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
verses.28:19: "All this in writing, by the hand of the LORD upon me, He made me understand—all the works of the pattern."
verses.28:20: And David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and of good courage, and do it; do not fear nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.
verses.28:21: And behold, the divisions of the priests and the Levites are ready for all the service of the house of God; and with you in all the work will be every willing man of skill for every kind of service; and the officials and all the people will be wholly at your command."
verses.29:1: Then King David said to the entire assembly, "Solomon my son, the only one whom God has chosen, is young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God.
verses.29:2: Now with all my might I have made preparation for the house of my God: the gold for the things of gold, and the silver for the things of silver, and the bronze for the things of bronze, the iron for the things of iron, and the wood for the things of wood, onyx stones and stones for setting, stones of dark luster and of variegated colors, and all manner of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance.
verses.29:3: Moreover, because of my delight in the house of my God, I have a personal treasure of gold and silver, which I have given to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house:
verses.29:4: three thousand talents of gold from the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of purified silver, to coat the walls of the houses,
verses.29:5: the gold for the things of gold and the silver for the things of silver, and for all the work to be done by the hand of craftsmen. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself this day to the LORD?"
verses.29:6: Then the chiefs of the fathers' houses, the rulers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the overseers of the king's work gave willingly.
verses.29:7: And they gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
verses.29:8: And whoever had precious stones in his possession gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, under the charge of Jehiel the Gershonite.
verses.29:9: Then the people rejoiced because they had offered so willingly, for with a whole heart they offered freely to the LORD; and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
verses.29:10: Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly, and David said, "Blessed are You, O LORD, God of Israel our father, from everlasting to everlasting.
verses.29:11: To You, O LORD, belong the greatness and the might, the splendor, the victory, and the majesty; for everything in the heavens and upon the earth is Yours. Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom, and You are lifted high as head over all.
verses.29:12: Both riches and honor proceed from You, and You hold dominion over all; in Your hand are power and might, and in Your hand it lies to make great and to strengthen all.
verses.29:13: And now, O our God, we give thanks to You and praise Your glorious name.
verses.29:14: Yet who am I, and who are my people, that we should possess strength to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from You, and out of Your own hand we have given to You.
verses.29:15: For we are strangers before You, and sojourners, as all our fathers were; our days upon the earth are like a shadow, and there is no abiding.
verses.29:16: O LORD our God, all this abundance that we have made ready to build for You a house for Your holy name comes from Your own hand, and all of it is Yours.
verses.29:17: And I know, O my God, that You examine the heart and take pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things; and now I have beheld with joy Your people, who are present here, offering willingly to You.
verses.29:18: O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our fathers, preserve this forever in the intent of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and establish their heart toward You.
verses.29:19: And give to Solomon my son a whole heart to keep Your commandments, Your testimonies, and Your statutes, to perform all things, and to build the palace for which I have made preparation."
verses.29:20: Then David said to all the assembly, "Now bless the LORD your God." So all the assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed low and prostrated themselves before the LORD and the king.
verses.29:21: And on the next day they offered sacrifices to the LORD and presented burnt offerings to the LORD: one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, together with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
verses.29:22: So they ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness. And they made Solomon the son of David king a second time, and anointed him to the LORD to be ruler, and Zadok to be priest.
verses.29:23: Then Solomon sat upon the throne of the LORD as king in place of David his father, and he prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.
verses.29:24: And all the leaders and the mighty men, and also all the sons of King David, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.
verses.29:25: And the LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and bestowed upon him such royal majesty as had not been upon any king before him over Israel.
verses.29:26: Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
verses.29:27: And the span of time that he reigned over Israel was forty years: seven years he reigned in Hebron, and thirty-three years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.29:28: Then he died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
verses.29:29: Now the acts of King David, from first to last, behold, they are written in the records of Samuel the seer, and in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the records of Gad the seer,
verses.29:30: together with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him, over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the lands.

notes.1:6: The Masoretic Hebrew here reads Diphath (and Rodanim in verse seven), whereas Genesis 10:3-4 reads Riphath and Dodanim, reflecting a common interchange of the similar Hebrew letters dalet and resh.
notes.1:46: Following the Masoretic qere (read form), Avith; the ketiv (written consonantal text) reads Ayoth.
notes.1:50: The Masoretic Hebrew here preserves the spellings Hadad and Pai, corresponding to Hadar and Pau in Genesis 36:39.
notes.1:51: Following the Masoretic qere (read form), Alvah (as in Genesis 36:40); the ketiv (written consonantal text) reads Aliah.
notes.2:7: The Hebrew employs a wordplay between the name Achar, a variant of Achan in Joshua 7, and the following participle meaning troubler.
notes.2:18: The Hebrew syntax is compressed, placing the marker et before both Azubah and Jerioth; it is rendered here as indicating that Caleb fathered children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth.
notes.2:50: The Masoretic Text reads the son of Hur in the singular, following the accentuation that joins it with Caleb before listing Shobal, Salma, and Hareph.
notes.2:55: The written Hebrew text (ketiv) reads a finite verb meaning they dwelt, while the traditional spoken reading (qere) translated here is the construct participle meaning who dwelt at, or the inhabitants of.
notes.3:17: The Hebrew term assir may be read either as an epithet meaning 'the captive' following the Masoretic accentuation, or as a proper name, Assir.
notes.3:22: The Masoretic Text names five sons after Shemaiah yet gives a total of six, likely reckoning Shemaiah together with his five sons.
notes.3:24: Translates the Qere reading Hodavyahu (Hodaviah); the Ketiv reads Hodyavhu.
notes.4:7: Translates the Qere reading ve-Tzohar (and Zohar); the Ketiv reads Yitzhar (Izhar).
notes.4:9: In Hebrew, the name Jabez (Yabetz) plays on the word for pain (otsev), a motif echoed in his prayer in verse ten.
notes.4:20: Translates the Qere reading ve-Tilon (and Tilon); the Ketiv reads ve-Tolon (and Tolon).
notes.4:41: Translates the Qere reading ha-Meunim (the Meunites); the Ketiv reads ha-Meinim.
notes.5:1: Reuben forfeited the privileges of the firstborn by defiling his father Jacob's bed (Genesis 35:22; 49:3-4), so the birthright passed to the sons of Joseph while preeminence and royal leadership passed to Judah.
notes.5:6: Chronicles spells the Assyrian king's name Tilgath-Pilneser (also in verse 26), corresponding to Tiglath-Pileser in 2 Kings 15:29.
notes.5:26: Pul was the Babylonian throne name of Tilgath-Pilneser III of Assyria; the Hebrew conjunction between the two names may also be understood explicatively as "even".
notes.5:27: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, verses 27 through 41 conclude chapter 5; most English translations place this Levitical genealogy at 1 Chronicles 6:1-15.
notes.6:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew versification followed here, 6:1 corresponds to 6:16 in most English Bibles, since the earlier Levitical and priestly genealogy is numbered at the end of chapter 5.
notes.6:11: The traditional reading (Qere) has "the sons of" before the second "Elkanah," whereas the written consonantal text (Ketiv) reads "his son."
notes.6:13: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "the firstborn Vashni, and Abijah," without the name Joel, who appears as Samuel's son in 6:18 and as his firstborn in 1 Samuel 8:2; many scholars take "Vashni" as reflecting "and the second."
notes.6:20: The traditional reading (Qere) has "Zuph," matching 1 Samuel 1:1 (compare "Zophai" in 6:11), whereas the written consonantal text (Ketiv) reads "Ziph."
notes.6:42: The Masoretic Hebrew uses the plural "cities of refuge" here and in 6:52, though Hebron (6:42) and Shechem (6:52) were the designated cities of refuge within these respective allotments (compare Joshua 21:13, 21).
notes.6:43: The Hebrew text here reads "Hilez," whereas some Hebrew manuscripts read "Hilen" and the parallel passage in Joshua 21:15 reads "Holon."
notes.6:46: The Masoretic Hebrew mentions "the family of the tribe, from the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh," while the fuller parallel in Joshua 21:5 also names Ephraim and Dan (compare 6:51–55).
notes.7:1: Following the Masoretic Qere (read tradition), "Jashub"; the Ketiv (written consonantal text) reads "Jashib."
notes.7:10: Following the Masoretic Qere, "Jeush"; the Ketiv reads "Jeish."
notes.7:23: The name Beriah echoes the Hebrew phrase for "in calamity" or "in evil," recalling the tragic slaughter of Ephraim's earlier sons.
notes.7:31: Following the Masoretic Qere, "Birzaith"; the Ketiv reads "Birzoth."
notes.7:34: Following the Masoretic Qere, "Rohgah" and "Hubbah"; the Ketiv reads "Rohegah" and "Jehubbah."
notes.8:6: In verses 6 and 7, the plural verb translated "carried them into exile" is resumed by the singular pronoun pointing to Gera as the one who led the relocation from Geba to Manahath.
notes.8:25: The Masoretic written text (ketiv) reads "Peniel," whereas the traditional read form (qere) followed here is "Penuel."
notes.8:29: The Masoretic Text omits the personal name of the father of Gibeon here; the parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9:35 identifies him as Jeiel.
notes.8:33: Saul's son Eshbaal and Jonathan's son Merib-baal (verse 34) appear in 2 Samuel as Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth, substituting the element "bosheth" ("shame") for "Baal."
notes.9:2: The Nethinim were hereditary temple servants assigned to assist the Levites in the duties of the sanctuary.
notes.9:4: Translated according to the Masoretic Qere reading, of the sons of; the written Ketiv combines the consonants into a single form resembling Benjamin.
notes.9:33: Translated according to the Masoretic Qere reading, exempt or free from other duties; the written Ketiv presents an orthographic variant with the same meaning.
notes.9:35: Translated according to the Masoretic Qere reading, Jeiel; the written Ketiv reads Jeuel.
notes.10:3: The Hebrew verb rendered wounded can also convey writhing in anguish or trembling in terror before the archers.
notes.10:10: The Hebrew noun here specifically means skull, distinguishing it from the general word for head used in verse nine.
notes.10:13: Saul's unfaithfulness uses the same Hebrew term applied to Judah's unfaithfulness in chapter nine, verse one, linking his downfall to the theme of covenant fidelity.
notes.11:11: The Masoretic Qere reads "the captains" (or "the officers"), whereas the Ketiv reads "the thirty."
notes.11:20: The Masoretic Qere reads "and to him" ("and he had a name"), whereas the Ketiv reads "and not."
notes.11:21: The Hebrew phrase literally reads "of the three, in the two he was honored," indicating that Abishai was doubly honored or more honored than the other two in his triad, yet did not reach the rank of the premier Three.
notes.11:44: The Masoretic Qere reads "Jeiel," whereas the Ketiv reads "Jeuel."
notes.12:3: Following the Masoretic Qere reading, Jeziel; the Ketiv spells the name Jezuel.
notes.12:6: Following the Masoretic Qere reading, the Haruphite; the Ketiv reads the Hariphite.
notes.12:16: Following the Masoretic Qere spelling for its banks; the Ketiv presents a slight orthographic variant of the same word.
notes.12:19: Following the Masoretic Qere reading, the captains (elite officers); the Ketiv reads the thirty. Literally, the Spirit clothed Amasai, an idiom for sudden prophetic empowerment.
notes.12:34: Literally, without a heart and a heart, an idiom signifying undivided loyalty and singleness of purpose.
notes.13:6: The Hebrew phrase literally reads where the Name is called, referring to the LORD's covenant Name proclaimed over the ark.
notes.13:11: Perez-uzza means Outburst against Uzza or Breach of Uzza, echoing the Hebrew verb and noun for the LORD's sudden judgment.
notes.13:13: Obed-edom the Gittite was likely a Levite from Gath-rimmon, a Levitical city in Dan assigned to the Kohathites.
notes.14:1: Following the Masoretic Qere reading, Huram; the Ketiv reads Hiram, the spelling used in Samuel and Kings.
notes.14:10: Following the Masoretic Qere spelling for the Philistines; the Ketiv has a minor orthographic variant with an extra yod.
notes.14:11: Baal-perazim means Lord of Breakthroughs, commemorating David's declaration that God had broken through his enemies like rushing waters.
notes.14:14: The Hebrew bekha'im denotes balsam or mastic trees, traditionally rendered mulberry trees.
notes.15:20: Alamoth is a Hebrew musical term literally meaning 'young women,' probably designating a high-pitched or soprano vocal and instrumental register.
notes.15:21: Sheminith is a Hebrew musical term literally meaning 'the eighth,' likely indicating a lower octave register or an eight-stringed accompaniment.
notes.15:22: The Hebrew noun massa ('music' or 'lifting up' of song) can also mean 'carrying' or 'transport,' linking Chenaniah's leadership with both the choral procession and the bearing of the ark.
notes.15:24: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads an unusual reduplicated participle (mechatsotserim) while the Qere simplifies it to the Hiphil participle (machtserim); both denote blowing the trumpets.
notes.16:3: The rare Hebrew word eshpar appears only here and in 2 Samuel 6:19; it is traditionally rendered 'a portion of meat,' though some scholars interpret it as a cake of dates.
notes.16:15: The Hebrew text here uses the plural imperative 'Remember' addressed to the congregation, whereas the parallel in Psalm 105:8 reads 'He remembers.'
notes.16:23: David's hymn of thanksgiving in verses 8 through 36 draws together passages from Psalms 105, 96, and 106 adapted for the installation of the ark in Jerusalem.
notes.16:27: The wording 'in His place' suits the tent David prepared for the ark in Jerusalem (15:1, 3), contrasting with 'in His sanctuary' in the parallel line of Psalm 96:6.
notes.17:5: The Hebrew concludes elliptically with 'and from tabernacle,' naturally understood as 'from tabernacle to tabernacle' in parallel with 'from tent to tent.'
notes.17:17: The Hebrew phrase 'according to the rank of a man of high degree' is difficult; it expresses David's awe that God treats him with the standing of an exalted person.
notes.17:25: Literally, 'have uncovered the ear of Your servant,' a Hebrew idiom for private, gracious disclosure.
notes.18:6: The object 'garrisons' is implied in the Hebrew verb here, matching the explicit wording of the parallel clause in verse 13.
notes.18:10: The Masoretic Ketiv and Qere differ only in full versus defective spelling of the infinitive 'to ask' (translated 'to greet'), with no difference in sense.
notes.18:16: The Masoretic Text of Chronicles reads 'Abimelech' and 'Shavsha' here, differing in spelling from the parallel names in 2 Samuel 8:17.
notes.19:6: Hebrew 'Aram-Naharaim' literally means 'Aram of the two rivers,' referring to upper Mesopotamia.
notes.19:16: 'The River' refers to the Euphrates, and Chronicles preserves the spelling 'Shophach' for the Aramean commander.
notes.19:18: The Hebrew reads literally 'seven thousand chariot' (charioteers) and 'forty thousand foot soldiers.'
notes.20:2: Hebrew malkam means "their king" according to the Masoretic vocalization, though the same consonants may also be read as the name of the Ammonite deity Milcom.
notes.20:3: The Masoretic verb literally means "and he sawed," though in comparison with the parallel in Second Samuel 12:31 it is often understood as assigning the captives to forced labor with saws and iron implements.
notes.20:4: Hebrew ha-Rephaim refers to the ancient race of giants; the singular ha-Rapha is used in verses six and eight.
notes.20:5: The Qere reads "Jair," whereas the Ketiv has "Jaur."
notes.21:1: Hebrew satan appears here without the definite article and may be rendered either as the proper name "Satan" or as "an adversary."
notes.21:15: Ornan is the Chronicler's form of the Jebusite name spelled "Araunah" in Second Samuel 24.
notes.21:25: Literally "shekels of gold, a weight of six hundred."
notes.22:7: The Qere reads "My son," whereas the Ketiv reads "his son."
notes.22:9: The Hebrew name Shelomoh ("Solomon") plays upon the word shalom ("peace") in the following clause.
notes.22:14: Hebrew be'onyi literally means "in my affliction," referring to the great pains and hardship David endured while gathering these materials.
notes.23:5: The abrupt shift to the first person ("I made") reflects King David's own voice in organizing the Levitical musicians and their instruments.
notes.23:9: Follows the Masoretic Qere "Shelomith"; the written Ketiv reads "Shelomoth."
notes.23:24: Whereas the initial Levitical census counted men from thirty years old and upward (23:3), David's final ordinance lowered the age of service to twenty years (see also 23:27).
notes.24:6: The Masoretic text repeats the participle ("taken, taken for Ithamar"), conveying the alternating selection of fathers' houses between the lines of Eleazar and Ithamar.
notes.24:23: The Masoretic text omits the name of Hebron—identified as the father of these four sons in 23:19—as well as the designation "the chief" for Jeriah.
notes.24:24: Follows the Masoretic Qere "Shamir"; the written Ketiv reads "Shamur."
notes.24:26: The Hebrew form rendered as the proper name "Beno" may also be understood literally as "his son" (compare 24:27).
notes.25:1: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere (read form), meaning who prophesied, whereas the Ketiv (written form) reads the prophets. Here prophesying refers to inspired musical praise and proclamation in worship.
notes.25:3: The Masoretic Hebrew text lists five sons of Jeduthun here while stating the total as six; the sixth son, Shimei, appears in the tenth lot in verse 17.
notes.25:9: Unlike the entries that follow, the Hebrew text omits the phrase his sons and his brethren, twelve after Joseph, leaving it understood from the twelve-member pattern of all twenty-four courses.
notes.26:15: Literally the house of the storehouses or gatherings, a complex of storage chambers associated with the southern area of the temple precinct.
notes.26:18: The Hebrew term parbar denotes an outer colonnade, portico, or western precinct structure adjoining the temple area.
notes.26:20: Following the Masoretic Hebrew text, which names the Levite Ahijah as overseer of the treasuries of the house of God.
notes.26:25: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere (read form), Shelomith, which also appears in verse 28, whereas the Ketiv (written form) reads Shelomoth, matching the spelling in verse 26.
notes.27:12: The Qere divides the gentilic into two words meaning "of the Benjaminites," while the Ketiv writes it as a single word with the same sense.
notes.27:24: "The chronicles" translates Hebrew divrei-hayamim, literally "the annals of the days," referring to the official royal records of King David's reign.
notes.27:29: Following the Qere, "Shirtai"; the Ketiv reads "Shitrai."
notes.28:12: "By the Spirit" renders Hebrew baruach, which can also mean "in his mind" or "in his spirit," understood here in light of verse 19 as divinely imparted revelation for the temple design.
notes.28:18: "The chariot" (merkabah) portrays the golden cherubim with outstretched wings over the ark as the symbolic throne-chariot of the LORD.
notes.28:19: The Hebrew shifts directly into first-person speech ("upon me") without an introductory speech formula, recording David's own attestation that the temple pattern came from the hand of the LORD.
notes.29:1: Hebrew habbirah ("the palace") is a term used in Late Biblical Hebrew for a grand palace-sanctuary or fortified temple complex; it recurs in 29:19.
notes.29:5: Literally "to fill his hand," a Hebrew idiom denoting consecration and the presentation of a willing offering to the LORD.
notes.29:15: Hebrew miqweh literally means "hope" or "expectation," here conveying the transience of mortal life with no lasting stay on earth.
notes.29:16: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads the feminine pronoun hi while the Qere reads the masculine pronoun hu to agree with the masculine noun for "abundance"; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.29:24: Literally "gave a hand under King Solomon," a Hebrew idiom expressing formal submission and pledged loyalty.
